newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 2.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Wednesday.
- All the main Irish taxes are generating more cash than expected, leaving finance minister Ruairi Quinn well postioned for his 1997 Budget.
- Four men and a woman appeared in a County Cork court on Tuesday night on charges linked with the seizure of a large cocaine consignment aboard a converted trawler.
- The Irish and British governments revealed plans to break the deadlock in the Northern Ireland arms decommssioning stalemate.
- Ten women and nine men were arrested by Irish police on Tuesday on suspicion of being involved in the murder of investigative crime journalist Veronica Guerin in June.
- Exploration company Celtic Resources said it plans to acquire a 50 percent stake in a silver, lead and zinc deposit in the Russian Federation.
- The plan to build a national convention centre in Dublin may not qualify for European Union funding if it is not completed by 1999.
- Property investment firm Dunloe House said on Tuesday it purchased industrial buildings in Dublin worth 11.1 million Irish pounds. IRISH TIMES
- Pro British unionist parties in the Northern Ireland peace talks are expected to reject a new initiative by the British and Irish governments to break the arms decommissioning deadlock.
- Shares in exploration company Pan Andean chaired by Irish businessman John Teeling tumbled from 115p to 40p in London on Tuesday due to disappointing drilling results in Bolivia.

- Irish Exchequer figures on Wednesday are likely to show that the government is set to undershoot its budget borrowing target. -Irish-based aircraft leasing firmGPA reported profit after tax and exceptional gains of $15 million for the three months to end-June.
- Over forty data processing jobs are to be created over the next 15 months in Tipperary, the minister for enterprise and employment said on Tuesday. -- Dublin Newsroom +353 1 676 9779
